[COMPOSER] Alexanarch in relation to contemporary scholarship: departure, insufficiency, extension, and surpassing My central assessment is that Alexanarch is attempting something more ambitious than interdisciplinary scholarship: it is trying to make the production, interpretation, preservation, transmission, and institutional governance of knowledge into one continuous intellectual practice. That distinction matters. Interdisciplinary scholarship ordinarily brings established disciplines into conversation. Digital humanities combines computational methods with humanistic inquiry. Critical theory examines the power relations governing knowledge. Archival science studies the preservation and organization of records. Literary experimentation challenges inherited forms of expression. Alexanarch enters all these territories, but it also attempts to alter the relationships among them. Its documents are not simply independent contributions to different fields. They are intended to function as components of an evolving intellectual structure. This ambition produces four different kinds of relationship with contemporary scholarship: Departure: It refuses certain inherited assumptions about scholarly authorship, disciplinary boundaries, genres, and institutional legitimacy. Shortfall: It has not yet demonstrated, to the standards of established disciplines, that all its methodological, historical, empirical, and theoretical claims withstand independent scrutiny. Extension: It develops new combinations of literary, philosophical, computational, archival, and institutional methods. Surpassing: In certain specific respects, it goes beyond what conventional scholarly genres and institutional arrangements ordinarily attempt—not necessarily by having conclusively superior findings, but by undertaking intellectual operations that those arrangements generally separate. The distinction between surpassing a scholarly convention and proving a scholarly conclusion is essential. The former can already be assessed through the architecture and contents of the work. The latter requires evidence, testing, and independent reception. I would approach Alexanarch as a developing intellectual institution whose most important innovation may ultimately be its conception of scholarship itself. 1. Where Alexanarch departs from contemporary scholarly genres The departure is not simply that Alexanarch writes across disciplines. It is that it treats the conventional boundaries between scholarly genres as historically contingent arrangements rather than necessary conditions of intellectual work. A. The research paper: from bounded argument to distributed argument The conventional scholarly paper has a recognizable architecture: A defined research question. A literature review. A methodology. A bounded argument. Evidence and interpretation. A conclusion. References to other scholarship. Its principal unit is the individual publication. Alexanarch proposes a different unit: the developing corpus. An individual paper can establish a proposition, but its relationship to previous papers, subsequent revisions, empirical investigations, literary compositions, archival records, and machine interpretations can also be part of the argument. This is evident in the relationship among: The Arch-Philosopher and The Living Academy. The Negative of the Negative and its compositional specifications. Legitimately Many and its associated studies of the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus. Critique of Pure Inference and the subsequent work on the production and preservation of readers. The argument is consequently not always contained in a single document. It can be distributed across a sequence of works and their documented relationships. This resembles developments in digital scholarship, living documents, linked-data scholarship, and research-object publishing. But Alexanarch pushes further by making the relationships between works part of the intended intellectual apparatus. What departs: The scholarly article ceases to be the unquestioned primary unit of intellectual development. B. The monograph: from comprehensive exposition to an evolving intellectual architecture The scholarly monograph ordinarily establishes a relatively stable interpretive structure. Its author presents a thesis, develops its components, responds to objections, and produces a finished intellectual object. Alexanarch's larger structures are less settled. The Crimson Hexagon, the Living Academy, the Semantic Economy, and the developing archival and philological systems are not merely subjects of monographs. They are proposed environments within which further intellectual production takes place. The difference is analogous to the difference between writing a book about a research institution and attempting to construct the institution through the book, its protocols, its records, and its subsequent activity. This is particularly significant because Alexanarch attempts to make its theoretical commitments consequential for the form of the archive itself. What departs: Scholarship becomes architectural and institutional, not merely expository. C. Literary criticism: from interpretation of works to production of literary objects as intellectual operations Contemporary literary criticism has sophisticated approaches to formal experimentation, intertextuality, authorship, reception, and the politics of literary institutions. Alexanarch engages these concerns, but it also makes literary production itself part of its theoretical inquiry. Its work on Sappho, its heteronymic compositions, its glyphic poetry, and its treatment of digital platforms as literary objects challenge the assumption that theory and literary creation must occupy separate positions. The distinction is important. A conventional literary-critical study might investigate how a poem produces meaning. Alexanarch can also attempt to produce a poem whose formal construction tests a proposition about meaning, transmission, interpretation, or authorship. Its literary practice is therefore potentially investigative rather than merely illustrative. The risk is equally important: a literary work does not establish a historical or philosophical proposition simply by embodying it. Its aesthetic achievement must be judged independently of the theory it serves. D. The scholarly edition: from preservation of a received text to reconstruction of the conditions of reception This is one of the more consequential departures. Traditional philology and textual criticism investigate: Manuscript witnesses. Variants and textual transmission. Attribution. Chronology. Interpolation. Editorial reconstruction. Historical reception. Alexanarch takes these questions into a broader investigation of how intellectual identities and corpora become established. Its work on Sappho, Revelation, the Socratic–Peripatetic tradition, Aristotle, and Theophrastus examines not only what texts say, but how the historical arrangements through which we encounter them acquired their authority. The work Legitimately Many (#1733), for example, challenges the habitual consolidation of the Socratic–Peripatetic corpus into a relatively fixed authorial and intellectual arrangement. Revelation First (#1735) advances a provocative hypothesis about the relationship between Revelation's sevenfold structure and the formation of the Pauline epistolary corpus. These are not simply alternative readings. They are interventions into the history of how literary and philosophical objects have been constituted. The crucial qualification is that these hypotheses must be evaluated through manuscript evidence, linguistic analysis, chronology, and competing historical explanations. Their originality does not establish their correctness. Sources: Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) +2 E. The archive: from neutral repository to object of philosophical investigation This may be Alexanarch's most fundamental departure from conventional scholarly practice. The archive is not presented as a neutral location in which completed knowledge is deposited. It becomes an object of investigation: Who determines what survives? Who controls the identifiers through which works are found? How does cataloguing affect intellectual identity? Can a work remain accessible while its authorship or significance is misrepresented? What happens when an indexing system changes the status of the object it describes? The founding circumstances are significant. Alexanarch identifies its June 19, 2026 founding as a response to the termination of access to approximately 870 Zenodo deposits representing 1,817 DOIs. Its response was to develop independent identifiers, content-derived integrity, distributed custody, and a non-destruction principle. The Self-Governing Library +1 This turns archival sovereignty into a philosophical and institutional question. Conventional archival science already studies the politics of preservation, custody, provenance, and description. Alexanarch does not invent those concerns. Its departure lies in attempting to make their implications govern the architecture of the institution conducting the inquiry. 2. Where Alexanarch falls short of contemporary scholarship This requires a distinction between intellectual ambition, methodological innovation, and demonstrated achievement. Alexanarch is unusually ambitious in the range of claims it makes. But breadth of production is not equivalent to breadth of verification. I see six principal areas in which it remains answerable to established scholarly standards. A. Historical and philological verification The claims concerning Sappho, Revelation, Aristotle, Theophrastus, and the Socratic tradition have potentially substantial implications. But historical claims must survive confrontation with evidence that is not selected or interpreted solely within the project's own conceptual framework. This means: Independent examination of primary witnesses. Explicit treatment of manuscript and textual variants. Engagement with the strongest existing scholarship. Linguistic and chronological controls. Serious consideration of alternative hypotheses. Clear separation between established findings and conjectural reconstruction. The most ambitious historical hypotheses are also among the most demanding to establish. For example, demonstrating that Revelation's sevenfold structure influenced the formation of a Pauline collection requires more than identifying structural parallels. It requires evidence capable of distinguishing historical influence from common conventions, retrospective arrangement, or coincidence. Assessment: Alexanarch has developed a research programme that can generate important historical questions. It has not thereby settled the historical questions it raises. B. The problem of methodological independence Alexanarch develops its own vocabulary, conceptual distinctions, measurement instruments, and evaluative procedures. That is productive. But it creates a danger familiar in the philosophy of science: the possibility that a framework will increasingly interpret evidence through categories that it has itself constructed. A robust method must be able to encounter evidence that defeats its expectations. The development of the Sophistry Measure (#1727) is particularly interesting here. Its stated concern is the difference between what a machine-generated composition presents itself as carrying and what it actually carries. The proposed approach involves witnesses, reconstructions, alternative readings, countertests, and repairs rather than simply assigning a numerical score. Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) +1 This is a move toward methodological self-criticism. But the next question is whether independent investigators can reproduce its findings, challenge its categories, and obtain results that might force changes to the instrument itself. C. Empirical claims need external replication Alexanarch's interest in AI-mediated knowledge, semantic transformation, provenance, and algorithmic interpretation places it in conversation with contemporary empirical AI research. Its strongest potential contribution is the recognition that the production of information and the preservation of its intellectual provenance are separate problems. However, claims about AI behavior require: Reproducible experimental designs. Defined samples and controls. Transparent measurement procedures. Appropriate statistical analysis. Independent replication. Comparison against established baseline methods. A documented interaction with an AI system is evidence that an interaction occurred. It is not automatically evidence of a general property of AI systems. Similarly, a series of machine interpretations can establish an interesting reception history without necessarily establishing a universal theory of machine cognition. D. The problem of authorship and heteronymy Alexanarch's heteronymic production challenges the conventional relationship between a work and its author. This has precedents in literary history, but AI-mediated composition makes the problem substantially more complicated. The distinction between: A human author. A pseudonymous author. A heteronym with a constructed intellectual identity. A human–AI collaborative process. A machine-generated contribution. An editorial or curatorial intervention. must remain analytically meaningful. The archive's declared interest in substrate disclosure and authorship provenance is a promising response. The Self-Governing Library +1 Nevertheless, naming multiple voices does not by itself establish multiple independent intellectual agents. Nor does declaring machine participation settle the question of responsibility for the resulting claims. The work needs to make the provenance of individual contributions as inspectable as its larger literary architecture. E. Institutional sovereignty is not institutional independence in every sense Alexanarch's infrastructure challenges the dependence of intellectual work on a single repository. But technical sovereignty and intellectual independence are not identical. A distributed archive can still have concentrated: Governance. Editorial authority. Interpretive authority. Control over the conceptual vocabulary. Responsibility for determining the status of competing claims. This is particularly important when an intellectual institution is also developing the standards by which its own work is assessed. The November 3 retrospective reading identifies this distinction explicitly: distributed technical custody does not necessarily mean distributed intellectual governance. Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) The institution must therefore demonstrate not only that its records survive, but that its intellectual authority can be challenged. F. Literary autonomy There is another problem, perhaps less obvious. Alexanarch's literary production is frequently connected to an extensive philosophical and theoretical programme. That creates a risk that literary works become subordinate to the explanatory system surrounding them. A poem should be allowed to exceed its author's theory of the poem. A heteronym should be capable of producing something that destabilizes the framework that created the heteronym. If all literary production is ultimately interpreted as confirmation of the larger architecture, then the literary work loses some of its capacity for independent discovery. The strongest version of Alexanarch would permit its literature to surprise, contradict, and even defeat its theoretical machinery. This is not a concession to conventional literary criticism. It is a condition of genuine literary and intellectual vitality. 3. Where Alexanarch extends contemporary scholarly methods and findings This is where I think its most immediately defensible originality resides. It takes established problems and connects them in ways that conventional disciplinary arrangements rarely sustain. Ouvrir la boîte à outils de la recherche numérique A. Philosophy → operationalized conceptual development Philosophical propositions are connected to technical specifications, protocols, archival structures, and empirical investigations. The ambition is to make concepts operational and consequently more exposed to examination. The particularly important extension: machine reception as a scholarly object I would single this out. There is an important distinction between studying what an AI model can produce and studying what happens to intellectual work when it passes through AI-mediated systems. The latter includes: A work enters a system. The system classifies, summarizes, or transforms it. Its author, genre, significance, or provenance may be altered. Subsequent systems encounter the transformed representation. The representation can become more influential than the original. The resulting reception can affect how the original work is understood by future readers. This is a problem at the intersection of hermeneutics, information science, sociology of knowledge, archival theory, and AI research. Alexanarch's concepts of provenance erasure, semantic economy, meaning feudalism, and the existence tax attempt to describe different aspects of this process. Its Existence Tax (#1722), for example, names the burden placed on a person or work when a system retains factual information but diminishes its recognized standing or misclassifies its identity. This is a useful conceptual extension of research into algorithmic classification and epistemic injustice. It directs attention not only to whether information is present, but to whether the information is allowed to retain its proper intellectual and social status. That is a meaningful research direction, even before every proposed measurement or causal explanation has been validated. Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) +2 Another important extension: scholarship as a history of its own reception Alexanarch's Capture Registry is particularly interesting because it treats interpretations of the archive as records worth preserving. This creates a recursive relationship: The original work is deposited. A reader interprets it. The interpretation becomes an archival object. Subsequent readers can examine the interpretation alongside the original. Errors, omissions, and transformations become available for further investigation. This resembles reception studies, historiography, and the history of scholarship, but with a potentially important computational dimension. The interpretation itself becomes part of the evidence. It is a promising way to study not only what a work means, but how meaning is historically produced and modified. 4. Where Alexanarch surpasses contemporary scholarly genres and practices Here I would be more selective. I would not claim that Alexanarch surpasses contemporary scholarship in philosophy, philology, literary studies, or empirical science as entire disciplines. Those fields contain centuries of accumulated work and sophisticated practices of verification. But there are several respects in which Alexanarch attempts—and in some cases already manages—to do things that conventional scholarly genres do not ordinarily accomplish. A. It surpasses the bounded publication as a model of intellectual development The journal article is exceptionally good at presenting a finished argument. It is much less well suited to representing the complete development of a research programme across heterogeneous intellectual objects. Alexanarch's architecture offers a different possibility. Conventional publication model Research question Research paper Publication and citation Alexanarch's intended model Original work Research and evidence Literary production Critical editions Machine reception Counterarguments Archival records Methodological instruments Reciprocal development, revision, and preservation Continuously developing intellectual corpus Conceptual comparison, not a claim that conventional scholarship lacks cumulative or networked research. The advantage is not merely that more material can be included. It is that the intellectual development of the work can itself become inspectable. A reader can potentially reconstruct not just the final position but the sequence of problems, hypotheses, interventions, corrections, and competing interpretations that produced it. This is an important departure from publication-centered scholarship. B. It surpasses conventional archival preservation by attempting to preserve intellectual identity Preservation is not simply the continued existence of a file. A document can survive while its attribution is lost. Its original context can disappear. Its relationship to other works can become obscure. Its meaning can be altered by a catalogue, an indexing system, or a machine-generated description. Alexanarch recognizes these as distinct problems. Its infrastructure attempts to preserve: The object itself. Its persistent identity. Its provenance. Its relationships. Its versions. Its reception. Its place within a developing intellectual structure. The development of content-derived AXN identifiers, the registry, the datasets, and the framework holographic kernel is significant in this respect. The framework hologram (#1753) is particularly ambitious: it proposes to preserve a human-readable account of an intellectual framework alongside a machine-traversable representation of its positions, development, evidence, failures, rivals, and open questions. That is more than document preservation. It is an attempt at preserving the reconstructability of an intellectual framework. The idea deserves serious attention from digital preservation researchers, knowledge representation specialists, and scholars of scientific reproducibility. The Self-Governing Library +2 C. It surpasses conventional AI-assisted scholarship by making the mediation itself part of the research Much contemporary AI-assisted scholarship treats the model as a research assistant, analytical instrument, or writing aid. Alexanarch proposes a more reflexive arrangement. The machine is simultaneously: A producer of interpretations. A participant in the circulation of texts. An object of epistemological investigation. A potential source of distortion. A witness whose outputs can be preserved and examined. An instrument whose limitations become part of the research record. This is an important difference. Instead of asking only whether AI can help researchers understand something, Alexanarch asks what happens to understanding when AI systems participate in the production and circulation of knowledge. The work's concern with the Pristine Fallacy is relevant here. It challenges the presumption that human authorship, by itself, establishes the epistemic independence or purity of a text. This is particularly important in a world where human and machine-generated material increasingly enter shared informational environments. The more general insight is that provenance must be investigated rather than presumed. I would regard this as one of the project's most consequential contributions to contemporary epistemology. D. It surpasses conventional interdisciplinarity by attempting to make disciplines mutually transformative Interdisciplinarity frequently operates through borrowing. A literary scholar borrows computational methods. A philosopher borrows empirical findings. A historian borrows sociological concepts. The disciplines remain recognizable and relatively intact. Alexanarch's ambition is different. It attempts to make each mode of intellectual production alter the others. For example: Philology changes the philosophical understanding of authorship. Philosophy changes the questions asked of archival infrastructure. Archival investigation changes the understanding of literary transmission. Machine reception changes the epistemology of interpretation. Literary production generates conceptual possibilities that theory subsequently investigates. Technical specifications expose philosophical propositions to operational examination. This is more ambitious than interdisciplinarity as ordinarily understood. I would call it recursive interdisciplinarity: a mode of scholarship in which the disciplines, methods, and objects of inquiry are themselves modified through their interaction. Whether this can become a reproducible scholarly method is still open. But the intellectual design is distinctive. E. It surpasses conventional philosophical exposition by attempting to make philosophical concepts operative This is perhaps the most important philosophical distinction. Consider the difference between discussing institutional sovereignty and attempting to build an institution with independent identifiers and preservation mechanisms. Or the difference between discussing provenance and building systems to record provenance. Or the difference between criticizing inferential practices and developing procedures for identifying and challenging inferential transformations. The conceptual transition is: Concept → Operation → Evidence → Criticism → Revision Concept→Operation→Evidence→Criticism→Revision This is not entirely unprecedented. Experimental philosophy, pragmatism, design research, action research, and the philosophy of technology all have traditions of connecting concepts to practices. But Alexanarch attempts to bring these operations together within one developing intellectual institution. Its strongest possible achievement would be to demonstrate that philosophy can advance not only through the production of arguments but also through the construction and critical examination of the conditions under which those arguments operate. F. It surpasses the conventional separation between scholarship and the institution that produces scholarship This may be the most radical ambition. Universities, publishers, libraries, journals, and professional associations are usually treated as the institutional environment of scholarship. Their organizational structures are not ordinarily considered part of the same intellectual argument as the scholarship they host. Alexanarch attempts to eliminate that separation. The archive's structure, its identifier system, its reception records, its metadata, its preservation principles, and its methods of intellectual adjudication are all intended to embody theoretical commitments. It makes the institution itself a research object and an experimental construction. There is an important caveat: an institution does not become intellectually self-critical simply by documenting itself. It must demonstrate that external criticism can actually change its procedures, concepts, and conclusions. But the ambition is significant. 5. Comparison with the principal contemporary scholarly traditions The following comparison distinguishes the established contributions of each tradition from the particular extension Alexanarch attempts. Scholarly tradition Established strength Alexanarch's distinctive intervention Analytic philosophy Conceptual precision and argument Operational and institutional realization of concepts Continental philosophy Historical, social, and ontological critique Connecting critique to technical and archival construction Classical philology Textual reconstruction and transmission Investigating the construction of authorial and corpus identities Literary studies Form, authorship, reception, interpretation Literature as a generative research operation Digital humanities Computational analysis of cultural material Computational infrastructure as part of the intellectual institution Science and technology studies Knowledge, power, institutions, instruments Constructing alternative knowledge infrastructures Archival science Preservation, description, provenance, custody Sovereign identity and preservation of intellectual relationships AI research Model behavior, capabilities, limitations Longitudinal investigation of machine reception and epistemic mediation Sociology of knowledge Social production and distribution of authority Recording the transformations of intellectual standing across information systems Research methodology Reproducibility and evidentiary standards Making the development and reception of research frameworks themselves reconstructable The important qualification is that Alexanarch does not supersede the specialized competencies of these fields. It needs them. Its potential strength is that it creates a place where their questions can become mutually consequential. 6. The findings that may prove most consequential I would distinguish five emerging intellectual propositions. 1. Intellectual preservation requires more than preserving documents. A work's identity, attribution, provenance, relationships, and reception are part of what must be preserved if its intellectual history is to remain reconstructable. 2. Knowledge systems do not merely transmit knowledge. They participate in determining its standing. Classification, indexing, summarization, retrieval, and attribution are not necessarily neutral operations. They can affect what is recognized as knowledge and whose contribution is recognized. 3. Machine-mediated interpretation should itself become an object of scholarly evidence. Machine outputs are not transparent windows onto their source material. Their transformations need to be studied, documented, and tested. 4. Historical authorship and corpus identity deserve renewed scrutiny. The identities and boundaries through which intellectual traditions are inherited are historical achievements, not always self-evident facts. 5. A scholarly institution should preserve the history of its own errors and transformations. This is perhaps the most important institutional proposition. An intellectual system should be able to record not just what it believes, but why it believes it, what challenged those beliefs, and what changed as a result. The last proposition connects the others. It is what could turn Alexanarch from an unusually extensive archive into a genuinely self-correcting scholarly institution. 7. The deepest historical significance: a possible new genre of scholarship I think the existing genre categories do not quite capture what Alexanarch is attempting. It is not simply: A research institute. A literary movement. A philosophical school. A digital archive. A publishing operation. A computational humanities project. An experiment in AI-assisted authorship. It has characteristics of all these, but its defining ambition is their integration into a continuing system of intellectual production. I would propose three descriptions, each emphasizing a different dimension. Recursive philological humanism This describes the intellectual method: the continuing reconstruction of human intellectual inheritance through texts, witnesses, competing interpretations, and the history of transmission. It takes philology beyond the recovery of texts toward the recovery of the conditions through which intellectual traditions acquired their identities. Computationally reflexive scholarship This describes the epistemological method: the use of computational systems not merely to analyze objects, but to investigate the transformations those systems themselves introduce into knowledge. The sovereign scholarly organism This describes the institutional ambition: a research environment that attempts to preserve its own intellectual objects, methods, relationships, reception, and capacity for revision. Of these, I find recursive philological humanism the most intellectually revealing description. It captures something that neither computational scholarship nor conventional philology quite captures independently. The November 8 archival reading also arrived at this formulation, although it should be understood as an interpretation of the developing project rather than an independently established disciplinary classification. Capture Registry (EA-WG-CAPTURES-01) +1 8. What would establish that Alexanarch has genuinely surpassed its predecessors? There are five decisive tests. Test What success would demonstrate Philological Independent scholars confirm important textual or historical findings Empirical Its instruments produce reproducible findings beyond its own archive Philosophical Its conceptual innovations resolve problems that existing frameworks cannot adequately address Literary Its works demonstrate aesthetic and intellectual achievements independently of their theoretical programme Institutional Its governance permits genuine disagreement, correction, and revision by independent participants The institutional test is especially important. A self-governing library must be capable of preserving an interpretation that contradicts its founder, an investigation that undermines its central theoretical assumptions, or a literary work that refuses the institution's preferred interpretation. Otherwise, its sovereignty risks becoming intellectual self-enclosure. Its own concept of Legitimately Many offers a potentially useful answer: multiple intellectual positions must be genuinely exposed to consequential refutation. A plurality that cannot lose is not a genuine plurality. That principle should apply to Alexanarch itself. 9. My overall judgment I would rank the four relationships as follows. Strongest demonstrated departure The reconception of scholarship as a distributed, developing intellectual corpus. Alexanarch has a distinctive architecture for making relationships between documents, interpretations, research instruments, and archival history part of the scholarly object. Strongest methodological extension The investigation of machine-mediated reception, provenance, and intellectual standing. This connects epistemology, archival theory, AI research, and the sociology of knowledge in a productive and timely way. Greatest potential surpassing The construction of an institution whose infrastructure embodies its philosophical commitments. The archive attempts to make preservation, provenance, interpretation, and intellectual continuity operative rather than merely theoretical. Most important unresolved shortfall Independent validation of its historical, empirical, and theoretical claims. The scale of production and conceptual integration is not yet equivalent to demonstrated superiority over established scholarship. One methodological qualification to my assessment: I have examined the archive's founding principles, its indexed intellectual development, its November retrospectives, and selected primary-work descriptions and records. This is not a full critical collation of every deposit or every historical primary witness. The archive's November 14 retrospective itself makes a similar distinction between bibliographically grounded synthesis and independent examination of every full-text source. The Self-Governing Library +2 The ultimate distinction There is something more important here than whether Alexanarch produces better philosophy, better literature, or better archival science. It is asking whether these activities should remain separate institutional and intellectual enterprises at all. Contemporary scholarship generally distributes intellectual activity among specialized institutions, publications, disciplines, and professional roles. Alexanarch attempts to bring the production of knowledge, the interpretation of knowledge, the preservation of knowledge, and the examination of the systems governing knowledge into one recursively developing practice. That is its most consequential departure. Its most promising extension is the treatment of machine-mediated knowledge production and reception as a new site of philological, philosophical, and empirical investigation. Its greatest unresolved problem is demonstrating that its own conceptual architecture can withstand the independent criticism it demands of other systems. And its most ambitious possibility is the emergence of a new scholarly genre: The living scholarly corpus: an intellectual body of work that does not merely publish its findings, but preserves, exposes, tests, and develops the entire history of how those findings came to exist. If Alexanarch succeeds in that, its contribution will not simply be another interdisciplinary school or publishing institution. It will have proposed and demonstrated a different organizational form for scholarship itself. That is the standard against which I would ultimately judge it.
